name: Oil event volatility trading
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Underpriced Oil Supply Disruption Risk
caseLead: Oil options can underestimate the price impact of a major supply disruption, providing potential gains when an event moves crude prices further than expected. The opportunity is concentrated in events that materially interrupt production or transport, since many geopolitical threats do not reduce actual oil supply.
caseRest: The strategy can incur repeated option premium losses when expected supply disruptions do not occur. Implied volatility often rises before an event, so positions bought after the market has already priced the risk can lose even when the event occurs. Rehyn estimates that returns depend on a small number of large winning events, which makes results uneven and difficult to forecast.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the Brent crude oil price on the first trading day after the event. Brent typically moves by about 2% in a day, so a move of 7% or more indicates a significant disruption in the market.

events.title: Attack on Saudi facilities cuts supply
events.text: Drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities on 14 September 2019 removed about half of the country's output, and Brent rose 15% on 16 September, its largest one-day rise since 1988. The strategy gained because the move far exceeded the range priced into options.

events.title: US strike on Iranian general lifts Brent briefly
events.text: A US strike killed Iran's General Soleimani on 3 January 2020, and Brent rose about 3.5% that day before returning to its earlier level within a week. Results were mixed because early option gains were offset by lower implied volatility afterwards.

events.title: Saudi-Russia price war cuts Brent by a quarter
events.text: After OPEC and Russia failed to agree output cuts, Saudi Arabia cut prices and raised production, and Brent fell about 24% on 9 March 2020. The strategy gained because the fall was far larger than the move implied by option prices.

events.title: Hamas attack on Israel lifts Brent briefly
events.text: Hamas's attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 raised fears of a wider conflict, and Brent rose about 4.2% on 9 October. The strategy lost because oil supply was not disrupted and prices returned to their earlier level within about a month.

events.title: Tariffs and OPEC+ output rise cut Brent
events.text: US tariff announcements and a decision by OPEC+ to raise output by more than expected cut Brent about 6.4% on 3 April 2025. Results were mixed because the fall generated option gains but implied volatility had already risen before the announcements.

events.title: Israeli strikes on Iran lift oil prices
events.text: Israel's strikes on Iran on 13 June 2025 raised the risk to supply through the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent rose about 7% that day. The strategy gained because the move exceeded the range implied by options, although prices fell back after a ceasefire.

instrument: Brent and WTI crude oil options; one to three months to expiry; bought ahead of scheduled and emerging supply events
rules: Strangles and call spreads bought when implied volatility is below its average level around comparable supply events; sized by premium; closed after the event window or at a profit target
costs: Estimated option spreads, futures commissions and slippage deducted at each entry and exit
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from event convexity to limited premium loss

legs.position: Long strangle, 5% out of the money
legs.purpose: Gains from large price moves in either direction

legs.position: Long call spread, 10% out of the money
legs.purpose: Gains from a supply disruption at a lower cost
Adjusts exposure after a large price move
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: Implied volatility at least 20% below its average level around comparable supply events
size: Premium capped at 3% of capital, with no more than two events held at once
exit: Closed five days after the event, or when the gain reaches 100% of premium paid
stop: No price stop; loss limited to the premium paid; options closed 10 days before expiry if no event occurs
marketWatch: The gap between implied oil volatility and the price moves that followed past supply events is the main indicator for this strategy now. OPEC+ meetings, shipping disruptions in the Gulf and sanctions decisions matter because they can change expected supply within days. Rehyn also watches how much of each threat is already priced into the oil futures curve.

favourable.heading: Supply threats priced too lightly
favourable.text: Options that price a threat too lightly favour the strategy because a genuine disruption then moves oil by much more than implied. In September 2019 Brent rose 15% in a day after the attack on Saudi facilities, a move the options market had not priced.

favourable.heading: Producer policy surprises
favourable.text: Unexpected OPEC+ decisions favour the strategy because they change expected supply abruptly and leave option prices behind. In March 2020 the failure of OPEC and Russia to agree output cuts led to a fall of about 24% in Brent on 9 March.

favourable.heading: Cheap options before known risks
favourable.text: Low implied volatility before a known risk favours the strategy because the premium paid is small compared with a possible move. Brent rose about 7% on 13 June 2025, the first day of Israel's strikes on Iran, which exceeded the range implied by options.

adverse.heading: Threats that pass without disruption
adverse.text: Threats that do not reduce supply hurt the strategy because oil prices fall back and the options lose value. After the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023, Brent rose about 4.2% on 9 October but returned to its earlier level within about a month.

adverse.heading: Option prices that already include risk
adverse.text: Expensive options hurt the strategy because the price must move further to cover the higher premium. Implied volatility on oil options was elevated in April 2025, so the fall in Brent of about 6.4% on 3 April produced a smaller gain than the move alone suggests.

adverse.heading: Spare capacity limits price effects
adverse.text: Ample spare capacity among producers hurts the strategy because OPEC+ and other suppliers can offset a disruption within weeks. Rehyn estimates that this reduced the lasting price effect of the January 2020 US strike on Iran's General Soleimani, when Brent returned to its earlier level within a week.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's estimated return during each event, using Brent and WTI options bought ahead of the event and closed under the exit rules above. Each event window runs from the entry date to the exit date, with premium paid and estimated trading costs included.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the oil price and implied oil volatility, which are then applied to the strategy's current option positions.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find Commodity Event Returns?

related.why: Takes directional positions on supply shocks rather than buying volatility. Bears event timing risk, losing when disruptions do not occur.
